quests.instruction: What is the action word for offering an idea for someone to think about?
quests.question: Suggest
quests.hint: Think about what you say when you have an idea for a fun game to play.
quests.explanation: Suggest means to offer an idea. We suggest a fun game for everyone to try!
quests.funFact: Suggesting new ideas is a great way to help a group decide together!

quests.instruction: What is the action word for telling someone that something is really good?
quests.question: Recommend
quests.hint: Think about what you say to a friend about your favorite book at the library.
quests.explanation: Recommend means to tell someone something is good. We recommend our favorite books to friends!
quests.funFact: Friends often recommend movies and books that they truly enjoyed!

quests.instruction: What is the action word for saying words to find out information from someone?
quests.question: Ask
quests.hint: Think about what you do when you want to know what time it is.
quests.explanation: Ask means to say words to find out something. We ask questions when we want to learn!
quests.funFact: Asking questions is one of the very best ways that people learn new things!

quests.instruction: What is the action word for replying to a question that someone asked you?
quests.question: Answer
quests.hint: Think about what you do right after your teacher asks the class a question.
quests.explanation: Answer means to reply to a question. We answer questions during class time!
quests.funFact: There is often more than one good way to answer a question!

quests.instruction: What is the action word for saying what you think is true, even without being sure?
quests.question: Guess
quests.hint: Think about trying to say a number without really knowing it for sure.
quests.explanation: Guess means to say what you think, even without being sure. We guess what is inside a wrapped box!
quests.funFact: Guessing games are a fun way to practice thinking carefully!

quests.instruction: What is the action word for creating a picture of something in your mind?
quests.question: Imagine
quests.hint: Think about picturing a magical castle in your head, even if it is not really there.
quests.explanation: Imagine means to create a picture of something in your mind. We imagine amazing new worlds!
quests.funFact: Imagining new ideas is how many wonderful stories and inventions begin!

quests.instruction: What is the action word for keeping something in your mind so you do not forget it?
quests.question: Remember
quests.hint: Think about how you know your best friend's name without looking it up.
quests.explanation: Remember means to keep something in your mind. We remember our friend's birthday!
quests.funFact: Practicing something again and again helps you remember it better!

quests.instruction: What is the action word for not being able to remember something anymore?
quests.question: Forget
quests.hint: Think about the opposite of remembering something.
quests.explanation: Forget means to not remember something anymore. Sometimes we forget where we put our keys!
quests.funFact: Writing things down on a list can help you forget less!

quests.instruction: What is the action word for finding something for the very first time?
quests.question: Discover
quests.hint: Think about finding a shiny shell on the beach that you never noticed before.
quests.explanation: Discover means to find something for the first time. We discover new things when we explore!
quests.funFact: Scientists discover new facts about our world every single day!

quests.instruction: What is the action word for traveling around a new place to learn about it?
quests.question: Explore
quests.hint: Think about walking through a new park to see everything in it.
quests.explanation: Explore means to travel around a place to learn about it. We explore new parks and trails!
quests.funFact: Explorers use maps to help them find their way to new places!

quests.instruction: What is the action word for seeing or paying attention to something small?
quests.question: Notice
quests.hint: Think about spotting a tiny ladybug on a leaf that others walked right past.
quests.explanation: Notice means to see or pay attention to something. We notice small details around us!
quests.funFact: Noticing small things helps you learn more about the world around you!

quests.instruction: What is the action word for watching something closely and carefully?
quests.question: Observe
quests.hint: Think about watching a caterpillar closely to see how it moves.
quests.explanation: Observe means to watch something closely. We observe animals and plants to learn about them!
quests.funFact: Scientists observe things very closely to learn new facts about the world!

quests.instruction: What is the action word for doing something again and again to get better at it?
quests.question: Practice
quests.hint: Think about playing the same song on the piano many times to learn it well.
quests.explanation: Practice means to do something again and again to improve. We practice reading every day!
quests.funFact: The more you practice something, the better and more confident you become!

quests.instruction: What is the action word for looking closely at something to learn about it?
quests.question: Study
quests.hint: Think about reading your books carefully before a school test.
quests.explanation: Study means to look closely at something to learn it. We study our spelling words for a test!
quests.funFact: A quiet, calm space can help you study and learn even better!

quests.instruction: What is the action word for gaining new knowledge or a new skill?
quests.question: Learn
quests.hint: Think about how you feel when you finally understand something brand new.
quests.explanation: Learn means to gain new knowledge or a new skill. We learn new things at school every day!
quests.funFact: Your amazing brain is always ready to learn something new!

quests.instruction: What is the action word for helping someone else learn something new?
quests.question: Teach
quests.hint: Think about what your teacher does at the front of your classroom.
quests.explanation: Teach means to help someone learn something new. Teachers teach us to read and count!
quests.funFact: You can teach a friend something new that you learned, too!

quests.instruction: What is the action word for saying or writing the letters of a word in the right order?
quests.question: Spell
quests.hint: Think about saying each letter of your name one at a time.
quests.explanation: Spell means to say or write the letters of a word in order. We spell our names and favorite words!
quests.funFact: Learning to spell helps you become a great reader and writer!

quests.instruction: What is the action word for finding out the size, length, or amount of something?
quests.question: Measure
quests.hint: Think about using a ruler to find out how long your pencil is.
quests.explanation: Measure means to find out the size or amount of something. We measure how tall we are growing!
quests.funFact: People use tools like rulers and scales to measure things accurately!

quests.instruction: What is the action word for looking at two things to see how they are alike or different?
quests.question: Compare
quests.hint: Think about holding two apples to see which one is bigger.
quests.explanation: Compare means to look at two things to see how they differ. We compare the sizes of two toys!
quests.funFact: Comparing things helps you notice interesting details you might miss otherwise!

quests.instruction: What is the action word for putting things in a neat and careful order?
quests.question: Arrange
quests.hint: Think about lining up your toy cars neatly from smallest to biggest.
quests.explanation: Arrange means to put things in a neat order. We arrange our books on a shelf!
quests.funFact: Arranging things neatly can make them much easier to find later!

quests.instruction: What is the action word for putting things in order so everything has its own place?
quests.question: Organize
quests.hint: Think about putting all your crayons and pencils into their own special boxes.
quests.explanation: Organize means to put things in order so everything has a place. We organize our toy box!
quests.funFact: An organized room helps you find exactly what you need in no time!

quests.instruction: What is the action word for making something new that did not exist before?
quests.question: Create
quests.hint: Think about building a brand new castle out of blocks that no one has ever made.
quests.explanation: Create means to make something new. We create art, stories, and towers of blocks!
quests.funFact: Every invention in the world began with someone deciding to create something new!

quests.instruction: What is the action word for planning how something new will look before you make it?
quests.question: Design
quests.hint: Think about drawing a plan for a treehouse before anyone builds it.
quests.explanation: Design means to plan how something will look before making it. We design our own art projects!
quests.funFact: Designers plan every little detail before something new gets built!

quests.instruction: What is the action word for thinking of a brand new idea or object?
quests.question: Invent
quests.hint: Think about coming up with a brand new game that nobody has ever played before.
quests.explanation: Invent means to think of a brand new idea or object. We invent games and stories!
quests.funFact: Many everyday objects you use began as a brand new invention!

quests.instruction: What is the action word for fixing something that is broken?
quests.question: Repair
quests.hint: Think about what a grown-up does to a toy with a broken wheel.
quests.explanation: Repair means to fix something that is broken. We repair a toy so it works again!
quests.funFact: Repairing broken things is a great way to take care of our belongings!

quests.instruction: What is the action word for making something work correctly again?
quests.question: Fix
quests.hint: Think about what you do to a wobbly chair leg to make it steady.
quests.explanation: Fix means to make something work correctly again. We fix things that are broken or wobbly!
quests.funFact: Fixing something yourself can feel like a very proud accomplishment!

quests.instruction: What is the action word for joining two things together?
quests.question: Attach
quests.hint: Think about joining two pieces of paper together with a small metal clip.
quests.explanation: Attach means to join two things together. We attach paper together with a paperclip!
quests.funFact: Attaching things securely helps make sure they do not fall apart!

quests.instruction: What is the action word for hitting a nail with a heavy tool to push it in?
quests.question: Hammer
quests.hint: Think about the tool a builder swings to push a nail into wood.
quests.explanation: Hammer means to hit something, like a nail, with a heavy tool. Builders hammer nails into wood!
quests.funFact: A hammer's flat, heavy head helps push a nail in with just a few hits!

quests.instruction: What is the action word for cutting through wood using a tool with a sharp, toothy edge?
quests.question: Saw
quests.hint: Think about the back-and-forth tool a builder uses to cut a piece of wood in half.
quests.explanation: Saw means to cut something using a tool with a sharp, toothy edge. Builders saw wood to build things!
quests.funFact: A saw has many tiny, sharp teeth that cut through wood bit by bit!

quests.instruction: What is the action word for turning a small metal piece to join two things tightly?
quests.question: Screw
quests.hint: Think about twisting a small metal piece around and around to hold wood together.
quests.explanation: Screw means to turn a small metal piece to join things tightly. Builders screw pieces of wood together!
quests.funFact: A screwdriver is the special tool used to turn a screw into place!
